messages:
ben: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the H100 pool during Canary A. Latency spikes for short seq (<64) when KV is cold; runtime is falling back to CUTLASS/CUDA and p99 doubles. Repro below, attaching logs.

taylor: Repro steps + logs pls? which model and batch config?

ben: model: redwood-7b, seq=16, batch=1, kv_cache_warm=false. Lifespan: cold start after cache eviction. Runtime chooses TRITON fused path but immediately falls back to CUTLASS due to a workspace allocation failure. stack trace mentions GPUAllocFailure + shared workspace exceed.

perf-bot: profile summary (10m window): kernel_route: TRITON->CUTLASS fallback triggered 42x on h100-canary; avg p99 +120ms when fallback happens. Breakdown: 65% fallbacks at seq<=32, 30% at 32-64, rest >64.

sasha: I vaguely remember allocator v2 having an accounting edge-case with temporary buffers during probeplan. If probeplan does a prefetch+memcpy for KV cold, peak resident goes up and can push TRITON over the workspace limit.

omar: can you paste the probe plan config used in canary? curious sample rate + seq cutoffs.

ben: here are the relevant bits:

```yaml
probe_plan:
  sample_rate: 0.05
  seq_cutoffs: [16, 32, 64]
  prefer_triton_on_h100: true
  kv_prefetch: true
```

ben: note kv_prefetch is on for cold path -> adds an extra memcpy and temp buffer.

deepa: that matches my suspicion. On KV-cold we do an extra prefetch memcpy into a staging buffer. Combined with TRITON's scratch buffers for fused kernels, peak workspace can exceed the per-device quota and runtime triggers fallback to CUTLASS which has lower scratch requirements but worse latency in our fused path.

taylor: quick idea: force TRITON for seq<=32 in canary to see if latency still spikes or we actually hit OOMs. But that could cause real OOMs for bursty traffic.

sasha: we have an env flag RUNTIME_FORCE_TRITON (test-only). I can run a controlled canary with reduced concurrency.

ben: did a short run with RUNTIME_FORCE_TRITON=true for seq<=32, batch<=2. Observed p99 improved to baseline for short seq, but OOMs appeared on larger batches (batch>=4) in the same pool.

perf-bot: new profile: OOM_count=3 (15m), TRITON_fallback_rate_down=90% for seq<=32 but overall stability degraded for mixed workloads.

omar: seems like we need smarter heuristics that include KV cache warmth and seq_len, not just hardware+model.

deepa: Agreed. Proposal:
  - Add kv_warmth signal to kernel-decider. If kv_cold -> bias towards CUTLASS (or conservative kernels) to avoid temporary buffer pressure.
  - If kv_warm -> prefer TRITON for short seq as it wins latency.
  - Add a hysteresis window (e.g., 30s) to avoid oscillation when warmth flips.
  - Reduce probe sample_rate for cold nodes so we don't trigger heavy prefetches during eviction storms.

ben: I like that. Also we should adjust workspace budgeting to account for transient prefetch buffers (estimating staging_buffer = k * keys * sizeof) so the decider has a more accurate peak estimate.

sasha: I'll add kv_warmth and transient_budget into kernel-decider. Implementation plan: add signal, feed from KV manager (boolean + last_access_ts), and modify scoring to subtract transient_budget when kv_cold. PR target: 1d for initial impl, then tests.

taylor: I'll set up a 6h canary with hysteresis=30s and new probe_plan (sample_rate=0.01 for cold nodes). Will monitor fallback_rate and OOMs. Tag me when PR lands.

perf-bot: created ticket PERF-4982 and alert rule: kernel_fallback_rate > 5% over 5m => page oncall.

infra-bot: rolling canary config template created: canary/kvcold-hysteresis.yaml

ben: Action items:
  1) sasha -> PR to add kv_warmth signal + transient budgeting to kernel-decider (1d)
  2) taylor -> run 6h canary with new probeplan + hysteresis, monitor fallback_rate & OOMs
  3) perf -> add regression alert on TRITON->CUTLASS fallback spike (done)
  4) ben -> write short design note with tradeoffs and inverse-case benchmarks

sasha: starting branch now. will link PR when ready. :thumbsup:

taylor: will kick canary once PR merged. tagging @ben @deepa on canary results.

ben: thanks all — main goals: eliminate noisy fallback spikes for short seq cold-starts without introducing OOMs for mixed-batch traffic. Keep canary tight.

deepa: small follow-up: we should also instrument kv_prefetch alloc size per-request and surface it in traces — will add to telemetry.

perf-bot: summary appended to PERF-4982: fallback root cause = transient workspace pressure from KV prefetch + triton scratch; mitigation = kv_warmth-aware routing + hysteresis + probe sampling reduction.
